name: Gas-installation verification and revision scheduler and register for ANRE EDIB firms
buyer: Small ANRE-authorised EDIB firms and installers who contract the periodic checks, plus building administrators and landlords with many consumption points
trigger: ANRE Order 179/2015 (consolidated 14 Dec 2025): verification at most every 2 years, revision at most every 10 years, only by EDIB-authorised firms. Firms must keep a current register per consumption point. The operator can cut supply the day it finds a missing check. Draft: revision replaces that year's verification.
existing: No competitor search run (budget exhausted). Distribution companies (Engie, Axpo, Gazest) publish the procedure and general ERP or field-service tools probably exist (unverified).
unchecked: Competitor search. Number of EDIB firms. Whether the distribution operators already run a free portal for results. Related to K02 (ISCIR workbench) but a different regulator and buyer; possible shared product.

first_check.duty: ANRE Order 179/2015 procedure (in force since 1 Jan 2016; amended by Orders 71/2020 and 96/2023; December 2025 consolidation published by Gazest). The final customer must have a periodic verification at most every 2 years and a revision at most every 10 years, plus after more than 6 months out of use or an incident. Only ANRE-authorised firms do this work (EDIB, or ET depending on pressure), recording it on a regulated fișă de evidență. The distributor or supplier can cut supply until proof is shown. Distributors must keep a database of the fișe that the authorised firms register. The Competition Council fined Delgaz Grid about 30m lei, partly for registering fișe late. The draft letting a revision replace that year's verification (profit.ro) is still unconfirmed as adopted. The Gazest PDF could not be parsed, so I took the article-level detail from secondary sources.
first_check.market: About 4 million gas consumption points (household and non-household; economedia, 2025), so roughly 2 million verifications a year. I did not find the number of EDIB-authorised firms: the ANRE public register exists but was not reached. Since each firm needs at least 3 authorised installers, it is plausibly several hundred to a few thousand firms (an estimate, not verified).
first_check.competitor: I found no dedicated SaaS for EDIB firms to manage clients, expiry dates and fișe after 3 Romanian-language searches. Flam Install (iOS, Innovative Sharks Dsoft SRL) is a free app for one firm's customers, with booking and payment history. Distributors keep the official database of verifications and revisions and send due-date notices. Distrigaz Sud Rețele runs an online portal for authorised firms, at least for commissioning requests. Large suppliers and distributors sell bundled verification services (Engie ASIGAZ), which competes for the end customer. Generic field-service or ERP tools: not checked.
first_check.reason: The duty is real. Under ANRE Order 179/2015 (amended by Orders 71/2020 and 96/2023), gas user installations need a verification at least every 2 years and a revision at least every 10 years, done only by EDIB-authorised firms. Each job produces a regulated fișă de evidență, and supply can be cut until proof is shown. I found no firm-side SaaS, only Flam Install, a customer booking app from one firm. Three things limit the opportunity. The distributors (Delgaz, DSR) by rule keep the database of these checks, and distributors and suppliers already remind customers. Big suppliers sell packaged inspection services (Engie ASIGAZ). The EDIB firms are small trades businesses that are hard to reach and pay little. I did not find the EDIB firm count. I could not confirm that the draft letting a revision replace that year's verification has been adopted.

challenge_check.killer: None found. The partial substitutes are the distributors' legally required database plus suppliers' free due-date notices to consumers, supplier bundles such as Engie ASIGAZ, and the single-firm Flam Install app. Generic field-service or CRM tools were not checked by name.
challenge_check.reason: Six Romanian-language searches found no dedicated software for ANRE-authorised firms to track verification and revision due dates or produce the fișe. Distributors must keep the database of checks, and suppliers send due-date notices for free. The Delgaz fine shows distributor-side registration is the bottleneck and lies outside a vendor's control. A Distrigaz Sud July 2026 guide sets the fields for the VTP form, so a form generator is feasible. The market claim is unverified: one secondary source cites about 5,700 ANRE-authorised firms of all types, but I found no EDIB count. The service is a commodity at about 100-200 lei, and suppliers bundle it (Engie ASIGAZ). The firms' margins are thin and generic field-service tools are a substitute. The idea isn't killed, but it stays weak.
